question: The regulation on packaging and packaging waste (PPWR) will take full effect in August 2026. However, certain requirements of this regulation pose implementation challenges for operators in the fresh seafood sector, where the use of insulated fish boxes is essential to protect seafood products from contamination, bacterial growth and other hazards.

These operators are particularly concerned about the reuse targets set out in Article 29 of the PPWR, which prove to be inadequate for insulated fish boxes, risk affecting the logistics chain and the viability of the sector and would pose food safety risks to consumers.
Importantly, the Commission’s impact assessment underpinning the PPWR did not assess specialised temperature-controlled transport packaging such as insulated fish boxes. 1.

Given that insulated fish boxes were not included in the impact assessment’s reuse modelling (switching tables, datasets, system assumptions), can the Commission state unequivocally whether insulated fish boxes fall within or outside the scope of the reuse targets set out in Article 29?

If the Commission considers insulated fish boxes to be within the scope, will it commit to adopting a delegated act that formally exempts insulated boxes in direct contact with food from these reuse target requirements?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.

2026) Under Article 29 of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)1, the reuse targets apply to transport packaging or sales packaging used for transporting products, in the form of pallets, foldable-plastic boxes, boxes, trays, plastic crates, intermediate bulk containers, pails, drums and canisters of any size or material, including flexible formats or pallet wrappings or straps for stabilisation and protection of products put on pallets during transport.

On that basis, insulated fish boxes fall within the scope of the reuse targets set out in Article 29 of the PPWR. The Commission is preparing the implementing act under Article 30 of the PPWR to establish a practical methodology for calculating the reuse targets, while further clarifying the packaging formats covered by Article 29.

Any consideration of an exemption for insulated fish boxes in direct contact with fresh fish under Article 29(18) would require a comprehensive assessment carried out by the Commission, considering the availability of reusable alternatives at scale.
In this context, the Commission is mandating the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) to issue a scientific opinion about food safety risks of reusable fish boxes, which should be delivered in 2027.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging
and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025.
